title: トランプ氏にNOと言わぬ日本、家康もぼやいた同盟の「実利と忍耐」
extracted_text:
「トランプ米大統領にノーと言えない日本」。こう題した英フィナンシャル・タイムズ（FT）の10日付の記事が話題を集めた。日本は対米依存に代わる選択肢がなくつらい立場にある、と指摘した内容だ。

トランプ米政権は同盟国に高圧的な姿勢を示す。西欧の首脳は公然と米国に不満を表明し、核戦力を含め自主防衛力の強化にも動く。日本とは対照的だ。

高市早苗首相は3月の日米首脳会談で「世界中に平和と繁栄をもたらせるのはドナルドだけだ」と持ち上げた。約束した対米投資5500億ドルの案件も積み上げた。

「こびた」という批判がある一方で、日本国内の世論調査では首脳会談を評価する割合が高かった。機先を制してトランプ氏からの無理な要求を封じたとして肯定的に受け止められた。

政府の同行者の一人は「中東情勢に関心が集まったが、会談の狙いは対中国だ。所期の目的を達成できた」と話す。5月に予定する米中首脳会談について「貿易でディール（取引）はあるかもしれないが、米国は台湾など安全保障で譲歩しない」との感触を得たと明かす。

現在の日米同盟は中国抑止の意義が大きい。トランプ氏の機嫌を損なわず、対中姿勢で足並みがそろえば日本には合格点だ。

トランプ氏が2期目で最初に対面した外国首脳はイスラエルのネタニヤフ首相だった。その次は当時の石破茂首相だ。米国も対中戦略で欠かせない日本を重視する。

防衛研究所の飯田将史氏は「米国の政治家や研究者と意見を交わすと、中国の覇権を許さないという強い意志を感じる」と語る。

同氏は欧州が対峙するロシアを「ディクライニング・パワー（斜陽の大国）」とみなす。「米国は欧州だけでロシアを抑止できるのではないかとみている」と分析する。米国が日欧への対応に差をつける背景だという。

古今東西、長く継続する同盟には利害の一致がある。16世紀の戦国時代、三河を領国とした徳川家康は西隣の織田信長と同盟を結んだ。

家康にとって東方の武田や今川などの脅威に備えるため同盟に合理性があった。織田は北の美濃や西の京をめざし、家康に東側の防波堤の役割を期待した。

力関係は信長が優位だった。家康は理不尽な要求に耐えた。遠い近江・姉川に自ら出兵し、敵国への内通を疑われた妻子の命も奪わざるを得なかった。

歴史家の磯田道史氏は著書「徳川家康　弱者の戦略」でこんな記録を紹介している。家康は「いったん信玄についた後、それを裏切って信長に属していたらもっと優遇されたかもしれない」とぼやいた。

家康も信長に自らの価値を理解させるのに苦労した。それでも感情を抑え、関係の維持に汗をかいたはずだ。信長は最後まで同盟の必要性を見失わなかった。

いまの日本も米国の要求に苦しみながら、自らの役割を認識して同盟維持に努力する。22年末に防衛政策を転換し、長射程ミサイルを保有した。26年には安保3文書を改定し、防衛費をさらに増やす大事が控える。

24年、岸田文雄首相は米議会の演説でこう訴えた。「米国は独りではない。日本は米国と共にある」。岸田氏は山岡荘八著「徳川家康」を読んでいる。

青年期に「律義者」と言われた家康は老年期に一転して謀略を駆使した。環境に応じて戦略は変える必要がある。いまの国際環境下の日本で能動的に「ノー」と言わないのはリアリズムだ。問題はそこに確固たる戦略があるかどうかだ。

（秋山裕之）

translated_text:
"Japan that cannot say no to US President Trump." This was the title of an article in the British Financial Times (FT) on the 10th that attracted attention. It pointed out that Japan is in a difficult position with no alternative to depending on the US.

The Trump administration takes a high-handed approach toward allies. Western European leaders openly express their dissatisfaction with the US and are moving to strengthen their self-defense capabilities, including nuclear forces. This contrasts sharply with Japan.

Prime Minister Sanae Takachi praised Trump at the Japan-US summit in March, saying "Only Donald can bring peace and prosperity to the world." She also accumulated $550 billion in promised US investment deals.

While there is criticism that this amounts to servile flattery, domestic public opinion polls showed high approval for the summit. It was viewed positively as having preemptively blocked unreasonable demands from Trump.

One government official who accompanied the delegation said, "There was a lot of interest in the Middle East situation, but the real purpose of the meeting was China. We achieved our objective." Regarding the US-China summit planned for May, they felt there might be trade deals, but the US would not make concessions on security issues like Taiwan.

The current US-Japan alliance is significant for containing China. If Japan can avoid offending Trump and align its China policy, that's a passing grade.

The first foreign leader Trump met in person during his second term was Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu. The next was then-Prime Minister Shigeru Yoshida. The US also sees Japan as essential for its China strategy.

Defense Research Institute expert Masashi Iida says, "When exchanging views with US politicians and analysts, I sense a strong determination not to allow Chinese hegemony."

He views Europe as seeing Russia as a "declining power." "The US seems to think Europe alone can contain Russia," he analyzes. This is the background for why the US treats Japan and Europe differently.

Throughout history, lasting alliances have aligned interests. In the 16th-century Sengoku period, Tokugawa Ieyasu, ruler of Mikawa, formed an alliance with his western neighbor Oda Nobunaga.

For Ieyasu, the alliance was rational for preparing against eastern threats from the Takeda and Imagawa clans. Nobunaga aimed to expand northward to Mino and westward toward Kyoto, expecting Ieyasu to serve as a defensive buffer on his eastern flank.

The power balance favored Nobunaga. Ieyasu endured unreasonable demands. He personally led troops to distant Anegawa and Akamatsu, and was forced to kill family members suspected of colluding with enemy states.

Historian Michifumi Isoda introduces such records in his book "Tokugawa Ieyasu: The Weakling's Strategy." Ieyasu complained, "I might have been treated better if I had betrayed Shingen and stayed loyal to Nobunaga."

Ieyasu also struggled to make Nobunaga recognize his value. Yet he suppressed his emotions and worked hard to maintain the relationship. Nobunaga never lost sight of the alliance's necessity until the end.


Japan today also suffers under US demands while recognizing its role and striving to maintain the alliance. At the end of 2022, Japan shifted its defense policy and acquired long-range missiles. In 2026, three security documents will be revised, with further increases in defense spending planned.

In 2024, Prime Minister Fumio Kishida addressed the US Congress, saying, "America is not alone. Japan is with the United States." Kishida has read "Tokugawa Ieyasu" by Sohachi Yamaoka.

Ieyasu was called "upright" in his youth but later became a master of strategy. Strategies must adapt to circumstances. In today's international environment, Japan's proactive refusal to say no is realism. The question is whether there is a solid strategy behind it.

(Atsushi Akiyama)
title_en: Japan That Cannot Say NO to Trump, Even Ieyasu Complained About Alliance's 'Practical Benefit and Patience'
